doc.title: Bobby Gordon interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997

title: Joining Leon Redbone and the plane crash
summary: Gordon met Redbone's associate Tom Waits at Condon's, joined Redbone without rehearsal for 17 years, appeared on Johnny Carson, and moved to California after a plane crash.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Because you can fit a lot of music on CDs as opposed to — records used to get about twenty minutes. You have also recorded with a whole number of people, including Leon Redbone. What was that like?
Well the first time met Leon Redbone was in Eddie Condon’s, I was playing there and he was looking for a clarinet player. And he sent in a fellow named Tom Waits, who

probably you are familiar with. So he was at the bar and I was playing the clarinet and I knew he was coming in, I knew somebody was coming in to hear me play so I said, “Mr. Waits, how do you do?” And he said, “I’m with Leon Redbone’s entourage.” So he had a couple of guys there. Leon wasn’t there. And Leon said that he did hire me. We were supposed to go to Cleveland and I got a good word from Tom Waits, and everybody else was there. So the next day I left for Cleveland, Ohio, and I went in the backstage dressing room and Leon was fooling around with the guitar and I was fooling around with the clarinet, and he said, “Let’s do it.” So we went out and I spent an association with him for 17 years.
I love that: “Let’s do it.” Just going out on stage, had no rehearsal.
No rehearsal or anything. But I spent the next 17 years with him, and recorded about five or six albums with him.
He’s got such a unique — what’s he like as a person?

He’s a very nice person. And he’s very nice to me. And we appeared on “The Tonight Show” on the Johnny Carson show four times in one year. And he always was nice to me. That’s the reason I moved out to California, because I left New York, Leon and I were in a — I don’t know if I should say — a plane crash together. We were in Allegheny Airlines going from Morgantown, West Virginia. We were playing at the University of West Virginia, and we were in a plane crash that crashed right after takeoff. And he was hurt and I was hurt and the best thing, we were in the hospital for about six weeks. And the best thing, that we survived it, there were a lot of people killed. And the best thing for me to do, the doctors said was go out to California. So I went out there and I’ve been out there ever since.
Wow. You were just talking about how hot it is out there now.
